title: proactive alert enrichment and responder scripting for incident-bot
author: Nora Patel
description:
Motivation:
We frequently get alerts that lack immediate operational context (recent deploys, relevant traces, recent error-rate spikes), which slows on-call TTR. This PR adds two complementary capabilities to incident-bot: proactive alert enrichment (pulls and aggregates quick context from traces/metrics/logs and SLO burn-rate) and responder scripting (small, auditable action templates that on-call can run from the incident thread). The goal is to reduce median investigation time and standardize initial recovery steps while preserving safety controls.

What this change does (single-string summary):
- Adds an enrichment pipeline that runs for new alerts and attaches a compact context summary: last 5 deploys, top traces (sampled spans), recent error-rate/time-series sparkline, and SLO burn-rate across the last 5/15/60m windows.
- Introduces a responder script registry: vetted, parameterizable scripts (bash/python) stored in the incident-bot service with metadata (required_roles, dry_run_supported, idempotency_hint).
- UI/Slack integration: enriched preview posted to the alert thread; scripts rendered as collapsible actions with a one-click "dry-run" or "execute" that performs RBAC checks and records audit logs.
- SLO-toolkit integration: enrichment tags alerts with a severity_hint computed from SLO burn-rate thresholds defined in the SLO toolkit config (consistent with SLO-alarms).
- Privacy & safety: automatic PII redaction rules for enrichment text and script parameter sanitizers; scripts run in a constrained execution sandbox via the existing runbook-executor shim (same sandbox used by canary jobs).

Files changed (high-level):
- cmd/incident-bot/main.go (wire new services, config flags)
- internal/enrichment/enricher.py (new enrichment pipeline core)
- internal/enrichment/redaction.py (PII heuristics + allowlist)
- internal/responder/registry.go (script metadata store + API)
- internal/responder/executor_shim.py (sandbox wrapper and audit hooks)
- web/ui/components/AlertEnrichedPreview.tsx (render sparkline and actions)
- integrations/slo_toolkit/client.rs (small adapter for burn-rate lookups)
- migrations/20260218_add_responder_registry.sql (DB schema)
- e2e/incident-bot/enrichment_flow.test.ts (integration tests)

Commits (summary):
- b12f4d3: wire enrichment service and config flags
- c7d9a9f: implement enrichment core, initial SLO burn-rate heuristics
- d4a1b2e: responder registry API + DB migration
- e8f7c44: responder executor shim and sandbox integration
- f01b3c2: UI pieces & Slack rendering

Migration notes:
- Adds a new DB table `responder_registry`. Migration is idempotent and backward-compatible; if migration is not applied, responder endpoints return 412 with guidance.
- New config flags (incident.enrichment.enabled, incident.enrichment.max_latency_ms, responder.sandbox.max_runtime_s) documented in deploy/CONFIG.md.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for redaction rules and burn-rate calculator.
- e2e tests run in CI against a local mock SLO service and a tiny sandbox image.
- Initial CI run failed due to timeouts in sandbox integration; fixed by adjusting test harness timeout and ensuring the sandbox image is pulled in the test step. Final CI status: pass.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy feature gated off by default.
2) Enable enrichment for internal prod only and monitor overhead metrics: enrichment.latency_percentile_p95 and enrichment.cpu_seconds_per_alert.
3) Gradually enable responder actions for trusted SRE group (RBAC gate).
4) After 2 weeks of internal canary, open to broader org.

Telemetry & observability:
- New metrics: enrichment.latency_ms{p50,p95,p99}, enrichment.lookup_failures_total, responder.exec_attempts_total, responder.exec_success_total, responder.exec_audit_events_total.
- Traces: enrichment pipeline emits a root span and attaches trace IDs to alert notes so downstream systems can link traces to alerts.
- Dashboards: added a short-lived panel in SRE dashboard for the rollout phase.

Security & privacy considerations:
- Redaction: default redaction removes tokens, emails, auth headers, and long UUIDs; teams can extend allowlists in config.
- RBAC: only users in roles listed on a script's required_roles can execute; audit events recorded to the existing audit-log-exporter pipeline.
- Scripts are stored encrypted at rest and validated by a vetting webhook that checks for forbidden syscalls/patterns.

Limitations & follow-ups:
- Enrichment currently queries only the tracing and SLO services; logs aggregation will be added in a follow-up (ENG-1331).
- Script sandbox is conservative and does not support long-running interactive jobs; we'll add a job-queue integration later.

References: ENG-1294 (linear), SRE-203 (on-call efficiency spike), internal doc: /docs/incident-bot/enrichment.md

If anything: this PR is intentionally split into a small core feature and a follow-up for broader logging and script templates. Reviewers: please focus on redaction heuristics and the RBAC enforcement path.

review_comments: Diego Morales (2026-02-19): Nice end-to-end. A couple of safety questions: 1) How do we prevent scripts from exfiltrating secrets if someone passes a leaked token as a parameter? 2) Can we ensure that the audit event includes the pre-exec scrubbed parameters?

Author (Nora Patel) reply (2026-02-19): Good points. We added parameter sanitizers (internal/enrichment/redaction.py) and the executor records both raw and scrubbed parameter fingerprints — raw params are never sent to the audit stream, only hashes and redacted previews. See executor_shim.py lines 120-165.
Anya Chen (2026-02-20): minor nit: the SLO burn-rate thresholds are hardcoded in the initial implementation. Can we plumb these from the SLO-toolkit config?
Author reply (2026-02-20): Done — added integrations/slo_toolkit/client.rs adapter and plumbed thresholds through incident.enrichment.slo_config_ref. Tests added.

Samir Banerjee (2026-02-22): e2e flake observed in CI previously — the sandbox image pull timed out. Looks like you increased test timeout; can we instead make the test pull the image in a setup step to avoid flakiness?
Author reply (2026-02-22): Addressed — test harness now invokes scripts/ci/pull_sandbox_image.sh in the workflow pre-step. CI rerun passed.
release_notes: Adds proactive alert enrichment (traces, SLO burn-rate, recent deploys) and a responder scripting registry; feature gated and rolled out to internal SRE first. Includes privacy redaction and RBAC controls.
